subject: platform/deploy
professional: a senior SRE / release engineer who ships self-service deploy tooling for other people's cloud accounts; first questions: do the generated artifacts parse and match their source of truth, are secrets handled safely, is the flow idempotent and does it fail honestly, and do the docs match what is built?

evidence.correctness: Ran `node --test platform/deploy/*.test.mjs`: 34 pass, 0 fail. Ran `node platform/deploy/build.mjs --out=<scratch> --why`: 1315 apps, 34 servers/*.json, ~12 skipped. Independent recomputation, none against code the author wrote: (1) sealedbox.mjs seal() output decrypted with PyNaCl (libsodium) SealedBox: plaintext 's3cret-π' came back exactly; (2) zip.mjs output opened with Python zipfile: testzip() None, names (incl. UTF-8 'dir/é.bin'), sizes and bytes all equal, empty file ok; (3) blueprintEnv() vs PyYAML over all 67 ventures with render.yaml: 0 key mismatches, and generateValue / sync:false / literal value flags agreed everywhere; (4) composeRepo for docker, fly, render across all 34 server apps (102 bundles): every compose.yaml parsed by PyYAML, every fly.toml by tomllib, every setup.sh executed under sh and wrote a .env with exit 0. Nothing was run against live GitHub, AWS, GCP, Azure, Cloudflare, Render or Fly (not permitted and not done), so the deploy path itself is unverified; capped at 3 for that.
evidence.completeness: Checked each README claim. Works end to end in dry run: catalogue from discoverSurfaces (1315 apps, README says ~1,230: stale), github-pages/aws/gcp/azure/cloudflare/android composition, render/docker/fly bundles, zip download, sealed box, footer/donate injection, deploy-iac-check.yml exists and runs tofu fmt/validate. README says 'Sixteen ventures' are server apps: build produces 34, and the 16 named are a subset. scaffold_static_deploy.py is in the directory but not in the README layout table and has no test. Cloudflare, Android, Render, Fly paths have no tofu-style validation and no live run (README admits Fly and cloud paths are unvalidated live). The browser Deploy flow in app.mjs was not exercised here; README says it was tested against a mocked GitHub API in a real browser but no such test is in the directory.
evidence.verification: 34 tests pass. Mutations seeded and reverted (git checkout, tree clean): M1 compose.mjs blueprintEnv `generateValue: true` -> false: 3 tests failed (caught). M3 zip.mjs central-directory offset +1: 1 failed (caught). M4 compose.mjs path-traversal guard in the static-provider loop disabled: 1 failed (caught). M2 catalog.mjs `all.length > MAX_FILES` -> `> MAX_FILES + 1`: 34 pass, 0 fail (SURVIVED: the file-count boundary is untested, only an oversize tree is). Gaps: app.mjs (all GitHub API orchestration, 250 lines) has no node test; scaffold_static_deploy.py untested; the tofu modules are only fmt/validate'd in CI, never plan'd; no test on the workflows' behaviour.
evidence.craft: Read build.mjs, catalog.mjs, compose.mjs, sealedbox.mjs, zip.mjs, app.mjs (deploy/gh), the cloudflare, github-pages and aws deploy.yml. Good: pure compose module shared by page and tests, shq/tomlStr/env-name allowlists, secretKey zeroed, nonce derivation commented, no third-party script. Defects: composeServerRepo / composeDockerBundle / composeFlyBundle repeat the same file-copy loop three times; in composeRepo `else if (rel.startsWith('tofu/')) out[rel]=content; else out[rel]=content` are identical branches (dead); composeServerRepo sets out['LICENSE']='' that the caller overwrites; app.mjs repeats the secrets/variables block four times (aws/gcp/azure/cloudflare); gh() returns null for any 404 on GET so a bad token on /repos/... reads as 'repo does not exist'; the catch handler says 'Nothing else was changed' right after a repo, secrets and files may already exist, then contradicts itself. Cloudflare template swallows `pages project create` failures with `|| true`. Actions pinned by tag, not SHA, in the generated workflows.
evidence.claims: Backed: 'tested against real libsodium output' (reproduced with PyNaCl); tofu/wrangler/Capacitor version pins (test + files); state encryption enforced; 'we host nothing and hold no credentials' (token goes only to api.github.com in app.mjs); disclaimer/operator notice in generated README and footer. Not backed or stale: '~1,230 browser apps' (1315 now); 'Sixteen ventures are processes' (34 built); Cloudflare blurb 'no card needed' is Cloudflare's policy, not checked; 'tested ... in a real browser against a mocked GitHub API' has no test file here; 'Not yet validated against a live Fly account' is honest. Hetzner/k3s: grep of platform/deploy finds no mention of it, so nothing here is misleading about the retired route. README never says this directory deploys the portfolio catalogue itself (that is .github/workflows/portfolio-pages.yml on Cloudflare), but a reader of the directory name alone could assume it; one sentence would remove the doubt.
evidence.fitness: Walked a visitor's job: pick an app, GitHub Pages or Cloudflare, paste token, Deploy. app.mjs uploads every file one by one through the contents API (PUT per file, up to 60+ commits sequentially), and the generated workflows trigger on push to app/**, so one deploy starts many queued workflow runs before the explicit dispatch; no retry or back-off on GitHub secondary rate limits. Apps over 60 files or 3 MB (the large flagship-style apps such as wall-framing-takeoff, shed-designer, sales-agent, sed-contra) are silently absent from the catalogue (reasons only printed with --why). Failure messaging is wrong as noted. Download path (zip, docker, fly) works and parsed cleanly. A person who just wants their own copy can finish; one who picks a large app cannot.
evidence.domain: Compared with ordinary SRE/release practice: positives are pinned tool versions, native encrypted OpenTofu state with enforced=true, per-provider budget files, concurrency groups, least-privilege `permissions:` on the Pages and Cloudflare workflows, destroy workflows, healthchecks. Departures: AWS path uses long-lived access keys as Actions secrets rather than OIDC role assumption; `tofu apply -auto-approve` on every push with no plan review; no .terraform.lock.hcl (acknowledged in README); state committed to the repo; actions pinned by tag; no rollback or previous-version story; uploading by per-file commits instead of a single Git tree commit (git data API) that a release engineer would use for an atomic publish.

defects.what: Deploy uploads each file with a separate contents-API PUT; combined with push-triggered workflows this starts many deploy runs and is slow and rate-limit prone, and the publish is not atomic.
Apps over 60 files or 3 MB are silently excluded from the catalogue, which drops most of the large flagship-style apps; the README does not list them and the skip reason prints only with --why.
Error handler claims 'Nothing else was changed' after repo, secrets or files may already have been created; gh() maps any GET 404 to null so auth or scope errors read as a missing repo.
AWS template uses long-lived keys and `tofu apply -auto-approve` on every push, no OIDC and no plan step.
Tests miss the MAX_FILES boundary (mutation survived), app.mjs orchestration and scaffold_static_deploy.py are untested; README cites a mocked-GitHub browser test that is not in the directory.
README counts are stale: '~1,230 apps' (1315 built) and 'Sixteen ventures' (34 server apps built).
Duplicated server-bundle loops, identical if/else branches in composeRepo, redundant LICENSE='' assignment, four copies of the secrets block in app.mjs.
Cloudflare workflow hides `pages project create` failures with `|| true`; scaffold_static_deploy.py is undocumented in the README layout table.

verdict: The core is sound and checkable: sealed boxes decrypt under libsodium, zips open under Python, blueprint parsing agrees with PyYAML on all 67 blueprints, and all 102 generated docker/fly/render bundles parse and run their setup script; 34 tests pass and three of four seeded mutations were caught. It falls short of a senior release engineer's bar on verification (the file-limit mutation survived and the GitHub-calling page code has no test), on claims (README app and server counts are stale, a cited browser test is absent) and on fitness and domain (per-file commit upload triggers many runs, large apps are silently excluded, AWS uses static keys with auto-approve, the failure message is untrue). Nothing in the directory refers to the retired Hetzner/k3s route, and the directory is for visitors' self-deploys, not the portfolio's own Cloudflare hosting, so it is not misleading on that point, though the README could say so in one line. Scores are the state before any fix.
